purpose: Determine whether 2022-2025 can share one leakage-safe player-week practice-state contract after adding a deterministic stable-identity dictionary for official-name aliases. This remains source qualification only and does not fit or score V09B.
reason_for_new_version: V1 failed its frozen 2022 bidirectional stable-identity gate at 97.5365% because exact official/canonical names differed for recurring players. V2 does not lower that gate. It adds nflverse's dedicated player master, whose primary key is GSIS and whose documented name fields include display_name, football_name, common_first_name, first_name, last_name and short_name. No v2 audit metrics were observed before this contract was written.

historical_state_sources.nflverse_injuries: unchanged from v1: canonical stable player-week injury/practice state
historical_state_sources.nfl_com_historical_pages: unchanged from v1: all 22 official NFL pages per season as independent all-position cross-check
historical_state_sources.nfl_reporting_policy: unchanged from v1: conservative official filing-day chronology
historical_state_sources.nflverse_schedule: unchanged from v1: game identity, kickoff and T-120 cutoff

identity_dictionary_v2.role_restriction: entity resolution only. Do not use latest_team, status, position, biographical fields, or any player-master field as historical availability state or model input.
identity_dictionary_v2.chronology_note: The master is allowed only as a non-outcome identity dictionary. Historical team/week membership and all availability state must still come from the target-season injury/report sources. A GSIS alias match is accepted only if that GSIS appears exactly once in the same historical season/week/team canonical injury rows.

identity_resolution_v2.normalization: same conservative suffix/punctuation/diacritic normalization already used by the qualified 2025 reconstruction
identity_resolution_v2.step_1: Attempt the original v1 exact-full-name or unique abbreviated-name stable-ID match.
identity_resolution_v2.step_2: For v1-unmatched rows only, normalize the official full name and compare it exactly against the allowed player-master alias strings.
identity_resolution_v2.step_3: Intersect every alias-matched GSIS candidate with GSIS IDs actually present in the same historical season/week/team nflverse injury rows.
identity_resolution_v2.acceptance: Exactly one GSIS may remain. Otherwise identity is unresolved and fails closed.
prohibited_matching: manual player-specific alias overrides chosen after seeing the audit
practice status, game status or injury text used to pick between identities
current/latest team used to infer historical team membership
position used as the deciding identity key
game outcomes, snaps, participation or completed-2026 outcomes
identity_resolution_v2.ambiguous_policy: unknown/unresolved; never pick the closest candidate

canonical_state_contract.unknown_policy: missing, unrecognized, late, ambiguous, or otherwise unqualified state remains unknown; never infer healthy/active
canonical_state_contract.source_effective_time: official Game Status Report filing day at 23:59:59 America/New_York, derived from scheduled game weekday
canonical_state_contract.date_modified_role: diagnostic parseability/source-integrity evidence for legacy 2022-2024 only

decision_rule: V2 qualifies only if every frozen gate passes in every target season. Passing qualifies only the shared source/state contract. It does not retroactively change V09B's historical disposition, fit V09B, authorize a probability feature, or change production.
no_rescue_policy: Do not lower gates, add fuzzy/manual aliases after seeing v2 results, use source status fields to choose identities, reinterpret absence as healthy, or inspect model/game/completed-2026 outcomes to rescue v2. Any materially different identity/state design requires v3.
